sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Mauryan Empire, c. 323 to 185 BCE
sources.note: Direct institutional essay, paragraphs on Chandragupta, Bindusara, Pataliputra and Ashoka. Greek diplomat's wall/tower numbers are attributed, not assumed exact. The disputed Arthashastra authorship is omitted.

sources.title: Livius: Ashoka's Rock Edicts, translation of the inscriptions
sources.note: Direct edition of primary text. Rock Edicts 2, 3, 9 and 13 on medical provisioning, wells, family respect, marriage/birth/sickness rites, and Kalinga remorse. Royal claims remain claims, not audited outcomes.

sources.title: UNESCO: Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi
sources.note: Direct institutional site. Ashokan pillar and brick core of Stupa 1; subsequent Shunga enlargement, Satavahana gateways and Gupta shrines explicitly distinguished.

sources.title: British Museum: fragment of Ashoka's sixth pillar edict, 1880.21
sources.note: Direct museum object record. Mid-third-century BCE burnished sandstone fragment from Delhi with part of sixth pillar edict. No unsupported transcription of this specific fragment.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: ring stone with goddesses and aquatic plants, 2000.284.10
sources.note: Direct museum object record, broad third to late second century BCE date, Maurya attribution and possible jeweller's-mould function based on comparative gold-foil finds.

sources.title: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts: Inscriptions of Aśoka
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly edition, printed p. 12, gives romanized royal style Devānāmpriya Priyadarśī Rāja and gloss. Full PDF too large for web fetch. This is a modern transliteration of inscriptional Prakrit, not the original Brahmi letterforms.

sources.title: National Museum India: Edict of Ashoka
sources.note: Indexed original institutional description, medical treatment of humans and animals and instruction to obey parents and give generously. Direct fetch timed out; stronger primary-text edition used for specific detail.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Year One, South Asia chapter
sources.note: Direct museum publication excerpt describes trade and gift networks, highways, towns, coins, Brahmi, guilds and finance in sixth-to-third-century South Asia. Card labels these regional developments rather than assigning each to one Mauryan policy.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Shunga Dynasty
sources.note: Direct institutional essay dates Pushyamitra Shunga's overthrow c. 185 BCE and distinguishes smaller successor polity from entire former Mauryan realm.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Patna Circle: Pataliputra remains
sources.note: Direct official archaeological monument listing records wooden palisade remains of Pataliputra and identifies Megasthenes account; no exact tower counts treated as excavated.
